claims.statement: The application mounts GitHub, Linear, and Slack webhook routers, whose primary event routes are POST /webhooks/github, POST /webhooks/linear, and POST /webhooks/slack; Linear additionally exposes a GET endpoint for webhook setup verification, while Slack has signed command and interaction endpoints.

GitHub, Linear, and Slack read and verify the raw request body before parsing it, rejecting invalid signatures with HTTP 401; Linear also rejects signed deliveries with a webhookTimestamp more than 60 seconds from local time as stale replays.

Verified provider deliveries are recorded through EventLog with source, endpoint, event type, delivery id, and provider references, but recording is best effort and is not used by these routes as a durable dispatch queue or acknowledgement gate.

The event log resolves provider identifiers to internal user, workspace, repository, and pull-request rows where possible, suffixes event types with payload actions, conditionally suppresses Slack event storage for channels that do not publish events, and uses partition rotation with a two-day retention setting.

Workspace resolution preserves an existing thread workspace, then resolves a valid tag, Slack channel ownership, repository ownership, user default, and instance default; GitHub routing is exceptional because unreadable repository ownership propagates to the route rather than being treated as unowned.

GitHub verifies repository routability before event-specific work; depending on OPEN_SWE_UNASSIGNED_REPO_WORKSPACE, an unowned repository may be ignored, but a workspace lookup failure returns HTTP 503 so GitHub can retry rather than permanently dropping the delivery.

GitHub admission distinguishes supported issue/comment, PR, push, and CI paths: normal issue/comment agent work requires a registered sender and an Open SWE mention, while review-finding replies and activity on an agent-opened PR have dedicated paths; accepted work is scheduled as background tasks.

GitHub repository allowlisting permits all repositories only when both configured allowlists are empty, and an optional public-repository organization gate admits private repositories, internal bots, or active organization members before public-repository triggers run.

GitHub automatic review uses separate reviewer-thread state: first-review actions are gated by repository enablement, watched pushes only re-review eligible PRs with a reviewer thread and watch enabled, and an unchanged diff is represented by a settled success check instead of a new review run.

A GitHub review wake-up can produce an idempotent Slack notice: the notifier locates the active Slack thread, stores a notice key before posting, and logs a Slack failure rather than retrying the mutation.

Linear Issue create/update deliveries launch automations, whereas direct agent dispatch is restricted to non-bot Comment create deliveries that mention Open SWE; the route avoids known bot-message prefixes, resolves an explicit/comment-author/workspace-default repository in order, applies the repository allowlist, and schedules the issue worker.

The Linear worker uses a stable issue thread, keeps an existing workspace or selects the repository workspace, maps the triggering author through email with creator/assignee fallbacks, records Linear source context, can use a vision fallback for issue images, and dispatches structured input.

Outbound Linear failure notifications are separate from inbound admission: they load the active workspace's linear MCP tools, attempt save_comment or create_comment within 30 seconds, and deliberately never retry a comment mutation.

Slack resolves channel eligibility before normal routing, rejects ineligible channels, sends one claimed refusal for an external-channel app mention, and routes normal work only from directed/allowed interaction shapes including mentions, DMs, code channels, eligible follow-ups, validated edits, or allowed bots.

Slack deduplicates before scheduling work using remote ten-minute lock threads for delivery and message identities plus a local bounded cache; retry headers do not suppress an unseen event, competing redeliveries are ignored, and remote claim failure fails open.

For a Slack request known to address Open SWE, synchronous or background processing failures are converted into a reply on the original Slack thread with an error id, and the synchronous wrapper returns a normal response so Slack does not retry a request the user was already told failed.
Slack worker dispatch distinguishes explicit and ordinary follow-up work: explicitly tagged requests interrupt an active run, while other Slack follow-ups enqueue behind it.
A Slack-bound workspace takes precedence over a repository preference for a new Slack conversation, while an existing thread remains in its recorded workspace.
